notes: Textbook status: the NCERT Class XI prelims PDF on ncert.nic.in carries the line 'Reprint 2026-27' (February 2026) of the November 2022 rationalised edition. Two secondary news reports (March 2026) of an NCERT notice say new NCF-SE-based books for Classes 10 and 11 are deferred to 2027-28. I could not open the NCERT notice itself; treat the deferral as reported, not verified. In 2027-28 this file will need replacing.

Curriculum: CBSE moved Classes XI-XII to a 'Secondary Part 2' curriculum for 2026-27 (file Maths_SecP2_2026-27.pdf). Its Class XI content, unit marks and formative-only list read the same as the 2025-26 Senior Secondary document.

Formative-only topics (not in summative assessment) per CBSE 2026-27: practical problems on union/intersection of two sets; composition of functions; general solutions of sin y = sin a, cos y = cos a, tan y = tan a; principle of mathematical induction; polar representation of complex numbers, statement of the Fundamental Theorem of Algebra and solving quadratics with real coefficients in the complex number system; graphical solution of linear inequalities in two variables and of systems of them; general and middle terms of a binomial expansion; sums of k, k^2, k^3; normal form and general equation of a line; section formula in 3D; derivative of composite functions (chain rule); random experiments, outcomes and sample spaces. Outcomes for these are included with difficulty 'extension' and flagged in the statement.

Principle of Mathematical Induction is formative-only in CBSE 2026-27 but there is no PMI chapter in the rationalised NCERT Class XI contents (the 2022 rationalisation removed it), so no chapter/outcome is recorded for it. The existing competency MATH.reasoning.logic (Mathematical Reasoning, grade 11) is not mapped: that chapter was also removed in the rationalised book and is absent from the 2026-27 curriculum.

Whether some formative-only topics (e.g. polar form 4.5, general/middle terms, sums of k^2/k^3) remain in the printed textbook text is only partly confirmed: the contents list shows '4.5 Argand Plane and Polar Representation', but sub-section level was not checked.
Chapter 14 Probability in the rationalised book begins at '14.1 Event' (no Introduction/random-experiment section in the contents); the sample-space material is formative-only in CBSE 2026-27.

Assessment (CBSE 2026-27): 80-mark 3-hour paper, typology 55% remembering/understanding, 25% applying, 20% analysing/evaluating/creating; no chapter-wise weightage; 33% internal choice. Internal assessment 20 = periodic tests 10 (best 2 of 3) + mathematics activities 10 (10 Lab Manual activities: record 5, year-end activity test 3, viva 2 - breakdown given under Class XII and referenced from Class XI).
Prescribed with the textbook: NCERT Exemplar Problems Class XI and NCERT Lab Manual Class XI (editions not stated by CBSE).
Section titles are from the NCERT contents page; sub-sections were not recorded. Outcomes are written by me from the CBSE topic lists, not copied from the book.

Several existing competencies are tagged grades 12-12 (e.g. MATH.calculus.derivative-rules) but are used here because Class XI already teaches sum/product/quotient rules; the fit reflects the skill, not the grade tag.

outcomes.statement: Describe a set in roster and set-builder form and classify it as empty, finite, infinite or equal to another set.
Identify subsets, proper subsets and the power set of a finite set, and count the subsets.
Write subsets of the real numbers using interval notation and convert between interval, inequality and number-line forms.

proposed.name: Represent subsets of the real line in interval notation
proposed.why: MATH.algebra.sets covers set operations generally; writing and reading open/closed/half-open intervals is a distinct notational skill reused in inequalities, domains and calculus.

outcomes.statement: Find unions, intersections, differences and complements of sets and represent them in Venn diagrams.
Use the laws of set algebra, including De Morgan's laws and complement properties, to simplify or justify set statements.
(Formative-only) Solve practical counting problems using n(A union B) = n(A) + n(B) - n(A intersection B).
Form ordered pairs and the Cartesian product of two or three sets, and count the elements of a product of finite sets.

proposed.name: Form Cartesian products and count their elements
proposed.why: MATH.algebra.relations is about representing relations; forming A x B (and A x B x C) and counting n(A x B) is a prior, separately assessable skill.

outcomes.statement: Represent a relation from A to B as a subset of A x B, and state its domain, codomain and range.
Decide whether a relation is a function and find the domain and range of real-valued functions.
Sketch and interpret graphs of identity, constant, polynomial, rational, modulus, signum, greatest-integer, exponential and logarithmic functions.

proposed.name: Sketch and read graphs of standard real functions
proposed.why: MATH.algebra.functions covers domain/range and recognising functions; sketching modulus, signum, greatest-integer, rational, exponential and logarithmic graphs is a separate graphing skill.

outcomes.statement: Combine real functions by sum, difference, product and quotient, and state the domain of the result.

proposed.name: Combine functions by sum, difference, product, quotient and composition
proposed.why: No existing competency covers the algebra of functions or composition; MATH.algebra.inverse-functions presupposes it.

outcomes.statement: (Formative-only) Form the composition of two functions and evaluate it.

proposed.name: Combine functions by sum, difference, product, quotient and composition
proposed.why: No existing competency covers the algebra of functions or composition; MATH.algebra.inverse-functions presupposes it.

sections.title: Trigonometric Functions of Sum and Difference of Two Angles

outcomes.statement: Measure positive and negative angles in degrees and radians, convert between them, and use arc length = radius x angle.
Define trigonometric functions of any real number using the unit circle and determine their signs in each quadrant.
State domain, range and period of the six trigonometric functions and sketch their graphs.
Use sum and difference formulas to find exact values and simplify trigonometric expressions.

proposed.name: Apply compound, multiple-angle and sum-to-product identities
proposed.why: MATH.trigonometry.functions is broad (definitions, signs, basic identities); expanding sin(x+y), cos 2x, sin 3x and converting sums to products is a distinct, heavily assessed skill.

outcomes.statement: Prove identities using double-angle, triple-angle and sum-to-product / product-to-sum formulas.

proposed.name: Apply compound, multiple-angle and sum-to-product identities
proposed.why: MATH.trigonometry.functions is broad (definitions, signs, basic identities); expanding sin(x+y), cos 2x, sin 3x and converting sums to products is a distinct, heavily assessed skill.

outcomes.statement: (Formative-only) Find general solutions of equations of the form sin y = sin a, cos y = cos a and tan y = tan a.

sections.title: The Modulus and the Conjugate of a Complex Number

outcomes.statement: Explain why the imaginary unit i is needed and write complex numbers in the form a + ib with real and imaginary parts.
Add, subtract, multiply and divide complex numbers and find multiplicative inverses.
Find the modulus and conjugate of a complex number and use their properties.
Plot complex numbers as points in the Argand plane and interpret modulus as distance from the origin.
(Formative-only) Express a complex number in polar form using its modulus and argument.

proposed.name: Write complex numbers in modulus-argument (polar) form
proposed.why: MATH.number.complex covers Cartesian representation and arithmetic; converting to r(cos t + i sin t) is a separate skill (formative-only in CBSE 2026-27).

outcomes.statement: (Formative-only) Solve quadratic equations with real coefficients and negative discriminant in the complex numbers.

sections.title: Algebraic Solutions of Linear Inequalities in One Variable and their Graphical Representation

outcomes.statement: Apply the rules for operating on inequalities, including reversing the sign when multiplying or dividing by a negative number.
Solve linear inequalities in one variable over integers or reals and show the solution on a number line.

proposed.name: Represent subsets of the real line in interval notation
proposed.why: MATH.algebra.sets covers set operations generally; writing and reading open/closed/half-open intervals is a distinct notational skill reused in inequalities, domains and calculus.

outcomes.statement: Solve systems (and compound/double) linear inequalities in one variable.

competencies.why: Compound (double) linear inequalities are solved by apineq; systems of two separate inequalities are the new family aeineqs.

outcomes.statement: Model word problems (marks, temperatures, mixtures) with linear inequalities and interpret the solution.
(Formative-only) Graph linear inequalities and systems in two variables by shading half-planes.

proposed.name: Graph linear inequalities and systems in two variables
proposed.why: MATH.algebra.inequalities is one-variable algebraic solving; shading half-planes and feasible regions is a separate graphical skill and the direct prerequisite for linear programming.

outcomes.statement: Use the fundamental (multiplication) principle of counting to count arrangements and choices.
Use factorial notation and evaluate expressions involving n!.
Count permutations of distinct objects and of objects that are not all distinct using nPr and n!/(p!q!...).
Count selections using nCr and use nCr = nC(n-r) and the relation between nPr and nCr.
Decide whether order matters and combine permutations and combinations to solve multi-step counting problems.

sections.title: Binomial Theorem for Positive Integral Indices

outcomes.statement: Build Pascal's triangle and relate its entries to binomial coefficients.
Expand (a + b)^n for a positive integer n using the binomial theorem.
Use binomial expansion for numerical approximation and comparison (e.g. evaluating (1.01)^n or (99)^5).
Explain the proof of the binomial theorem for positive integral index and use it to prove divisibility results.
(Formative-only) Find a specified general term, a term independent of x, or the middle term(s) of an expansion.
Describe a sequence by its general term or a recurrence and write the corresponding series in sigma notation.

competencies.why: Describing a sequence by a recurrence relation is exactly what these families assess (terms from a recursive rule, and from a recursive rule to a formula); the outcome is mapped only to sequence-notation, so the recurrence part looks missing.

proposed.name: Describe sequences and series by general term, recursion and sigma notation
proposed.why: Existing sequence competencies are AP- or GP-specific; the general idea of a sequence as a function of n, recursive definitions and series notation is not covered.

outcomes.statement: Find the general term and the sum of n terms of a geometric progression.
Find the sum of an infinite geometric series when |r| < 1 and use it (e.g. recurring decimals).
Insert arithmetic and geometric means between two numbers and use AM >= GM.

proposed.name: Use arithmetic and geometric means and the AM-GM inequality
proposed.why: Inserting means and using AM >= GM goes beyond computing terms and sums of a GP.

outcomes.statement: Solve word problems (growth, depreciation, compound interest) using geometric progressions.
(Formative-only) Evaluate sums of k, k^2 and k^3 to n terms and use them to sum related series.

proposed.name: Evaluate sums of k, k squared and k cubed and series built from them
proposed.why: No existing competency covers closed forms for sums of powers of natural numbers (formative-only in CBSE 2026-27).

sections.title: Various Forms of the Equation of a Line
Distance of a Point From a Line

outcomes.statement: Find the slope of a line from two points or its inclination, and use slopes to test parallel, perpendicular and collinear points.
Find the angle between two lines from their slopes.
Write the equation of a line in point-slope, slope-intercept, two-point and intercept forms, including lines parallel to the axes.
Find the perpendicular distance from a point to a line and the distance between parallel lines.
(Formative-only) Convert a general linear equation Ax + By + C = 0 to slope-intercept, intercept and normal forms.
Describe circles, ellipses, parabolas, hyperbolas and degenerate cases as sections of a double cone.
Write the equation of a circle from its centre and radius and find centre and radius from a given equation.
Find focus, directrix, axis and latus rectum of a parabola in standard form, and its equation from given data.
Find foci, vertices, axes lengths, eccentricity and latus rectum of an ellipse in standard form, and its equation from given data.
Find foci, vertices, transverse/conjugate axes, eccentricity and latus rectum of a hyperbola in standard form, and its equation from given data.
Sketch a conic from its standard equation and apply conic properties to simple real-world contexts (arches, reflectors).

sections.title: Coordinate Axes and Coordinate Planes in Three Dimensional Space
Coordinates of a Point in Space

outcomes.statement: Identify coordinate axes, coordinate planes and octants in three-dimensional space.
Locate and plot a point from its coordinates (x, y, z) and give coordinates of points on axes and planes.
Use the distance formula in space to find lengths and test collinearity or classify triangles.
(Formative-only) Find the point dividing a segment in space in a given ratio, including the midpoint and centroid.
Interpret the derivative as an instantaneous rate of change and as the slope of a tangent, using distance-time data.
Estimate limits from tables or graphs and distinguish left-hand and right-hand limits.
Evaluate limits of polynomial and rational functions using limit algebra, factorisation and the standard limit of (x^n - a^n)/(x - a).
Evaluate limits involving trigonometric, exponential and logarithmic functions using standard limits such as sin x / x.
Find the derivative of simple functions from first principles.
Differentiate sums, differences, products and quotients of polynomial and trigonometric functions.
(Formative-only) Differentiate a composite function using the chain rule.
Explain why measures of central tendency are not enough and find the range of a data set.
Calculate mean deviation about the mean and about the median for ungrouped, discrete and continuous frequency data.

proposed.name: Calculate mean deviation about the mean or median
proposed.why: MATH.statistics.dispersion names variance and standard deviation; mean deviation (ungrouped, discrete and continuous frequency data) is a separate measure with its own procedure.

outcomes.statement: Calculate variance and standard deviation of ungrouped and grouped data, including by the step-deviation (shortcut) method.
Compare the variability of two distributions and interpret the result in context.
(Formative-only) Describe random experiments, outcomes and sample spaces using set notation.
Describe events as subsets of a sample space and form 'not A', 'A and B', 'A or B' events.
Identify mutually exclusive and exhaustive events.
Check whether a probability assignment satisfies the axioms and find probabilities of events on a finite sample space.
Use P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A and B) and P(not A) = 1 - P(A) to solve probability problems.
